_about: Settles names the build cannot spell from the Berean on its own (design 3.2). 'people': person id -> the Berean spelling of their name, for a person whose name lines carry no Berean-tagged word. 'aliases': extra forms that should land on a page (form -> Berean spelling). 'reviewed': hand decisions on TIPNR name lines (key 'person|Strong's|first form'): exclude with a reason, confirm a spelling with Berean verse evidence, or move verses away ('dropRefs'). 'identities': site-added people TIPNR lacks, with the Strong's number, spelling and verses the build checks. The build fails on any decision that no longer matches.

abinadab-1ki-4-11|H41|Abinadab.reason: The verse names Ben-abinadab, not a separate Abinadab; do not split a patronymic into another bearer.

achish-1sa-21-10|H40|Abimelech.reason: Abimelech occurs in the Psalm heading, not the numbered Berean verse; no verified verse occurrence for this name line.

sennacherib-2ki-18-13|H5623|Sargon.reason: TIPNR files Sargon (Isaiah 20:1) as another name of Sennacherib; the site's people data keeps Sargon as his own person (sargon-isa-20-1), who bears the Sargon page instead (see "identities"). Sennacherib keeps his own name line.

ahasuerus-ezr-4-6|H325|Ahasuerus.reason: Daniel 9:1 names Darius's father, whom the site's people data keeps as his own person (ahasuerus-dan-9-1: 'He is not the Ahasuerus of the book of Esther'); the verse moves to him. The king of Esther and Ezra keeps his other 28 verses.

sargon-isa-20-1.reason: Site-added person; the Berean prints 'Sargon king of Assyria' at Isaiah 20:1, and TIPNR's own Sargon line there gives Strong's H5623 ('Sargon, an Assyrian king').

ahasuerus-dan-9-1.reason: Site-added father of Darius the Mede; the Berean prints 'Darius son of Xerxes' at Daniel 9:1, the Hebrew name Achashverosh (H325) that TIPNR tags there. A separate bearer on the Xerxes page, not merged with the king of Esther.

candace-act-8-27.reason: Site-added queen; the Berean prints 'Candace, queen of the Ethiopians' at Acts 8:27 as her name, without an article (unlike 'the Tartan' or 'the Rabshakeh'), and Strong's G2582 treats it as a proper name ('Candace, an Egyptian queen'). Many think it was the title of the queens of Meroe; her person record says only what Acts says.
